task: Cycle 5 C5-03: 120m real-checkpoint hardware NVFP4 W4A4 perplexity and small-shape dynamic activation quantizer fusion on Blackwell

data.startup_verification: SHA-256 of every shard file and the manifest token / document checks (real_text_data.verify_manifest), before and apart from any scoring

kernel_parity.reference: micro_rotated_ptq rotation (FP32) + nvfp4_encode + pack_e2m1 + to_blocked; every case also checks the embedded C4-02 quantizer

part_a.design: Williams-balanced orders over all methods; CUDA events, mean of `iters` flushed samples per round (raw per-call times in event_samples_ms), 4x L2 flush before every sample; median over rounds. `wall_ms`: host clock between synchronizes. c4_02_* is the embedded pre-C5-03 quantizer, c5_03_* the current module; both allocate their buffers per call and share the NVFP4 weights and scaled_mm.

part_b.design: random-init BF16 weights, random tokens. NVFP4 variants replace every block linear (qkv, out, gate, up, down) by an RTN NVFP4Linear; bfly_b16 uses random angles, had_b16_static_gs scales calibrated on the timed tokens. c4_02_* wraps the same layers with the embedded C4-02 quantizer. Embedding, RMSNorms, attention (SDPA) and the tied LM head stay BF16. `_graph`: one CUDA graph per forward; bf16_compiled: torch.compile default mode.

analysis.endpoint: per-seed delta NLL (quantized - BF16) of the same checkpoint; contrast differences are x - y

postprocess.reason: Remediation of the C5-03 audit (audits/AUDIT_cycle5_c5_03_gpt62_astra.md, findings 1-5): the raw measurements of the canonical result 726b20c (measured by the clean commit 38cef48) are preserved unchanged, so test.bin is not scored a third time. part_c.analysis, summary and caveats are recomputed (the caveats now state the superseded 4736807 run and the measurement limits), and the result is checked by the hardened validator (calibration draw, linear parameter counts, kernel profiles, cooperative launch record, AWQ fields). The public launcher contract and the integer-view bitwise checks are verified live by the test suite and the audit replay. Nothing was retrained or re-measured.

caveats: Part C statistics have df = 2 (three paired seeds): the two-sided t-test has little power, and the exact sign-flip p-value cannot fall below 0.25 for any contrast, so no sign-flip result can be significant.

Part C uses one corpus (FineWeb-Edu sample-10BT shards, GPT-2 BPE), one calibration draw of 128 train.bin sequences (seed 20261126) and one model size: the 120m model trained 640 steps with muon_ps3_blackwell on one RTX 5080 (sm_120). Deltas may differ for longer training, other optimizers or larger models.
GPU training is seeded (initial state, batch stream) but not claimed to be bit-reproducible; the three checkpoints are retained outside git with their tensor and file SHA-256 values.

test.bin is held out from every selection rule of this run (Phase 2 maps it after the freeze), but the same test.bin was scored by earlier cycles on other checkpoints; it is not a study-level unseen holdout.

AWQ alpha is chosen per seed on val.bin with live hardware W4A4 dynamic scoring; an alpha = 0 choice makes the AWQ rows copies of the plain rotation + GPTQ rows (counted as inherited, not as measurements).

Part A/B weights and activations are random; latency does not depend on values. A 4x L2 flush before every sample makes the activation come from DRAM, which is pessimistic for a layer whose input was just written by the previous kernel.
CUDA-event resolution on this GPU is about 2 us; per-round values are means of `iters` flushed calls and the reported value is the median over Williams rounds.
bf16_compiled is torch.compile(default); NVFP4 models run eager or as CUDA graphs, not compiled.

The cooperative single-launch quantizer (ablation) is bit-exact and survives repeated graph replays but is slower than the two-pass PDL quantizer, so it is not enabled; a single-program fused quantizer was measured during development at 10-25x slower and dropped.

Static-scale (had_b16_static_gs) differences against C4-02 are near parity: their sign changes between shapes and between sessions, so no static-scale speedup is claimed. Eager full-forward (Part B) times vary more between sessions than the CUDA-graph ratios do; the graph ratios are the reproducible latency result.

Study history: a superseded canonical run at commit 4736807 scored the same test.bin before host launch-plan caching was added at 38cef48; this result is the complete rerun at 38cef48. Both runs (logs and the superseded JSON) are retained in artifacts/c5_03_run_evidence/ with pinned SHA-256 values, and test.bin was also scored by earlier cycles, so the test scores here are not a first look at an unseen holdout.
C5-03 W4A4 (CUDA graph) still trails BF16 cuBLAS for: had_b16 at (1024,512,1408) 0.0240 ms vs bf16 0.0230 ms; bfly_b16 at (1024,512,1408) 0.0261 ms vs bf16 0.0230 ms.
C5-03 is not faster than C4-02 (CUDA graph median) for: had_b16_static_gs at (16,4096,4096).
AWQ selected alpha = 0 in 0 of 6 (seed, method) cases; those rows are inherited copies.
